body.x: Passwords, text-message codes and one-time passwords all ask the user to type something in or complete a separate step. They also say little about whether the person approving a payment is really the account holder, a question that matters more when synthetic voices and replayed recordings can imitate a speaker.
What if the moment of approval could check that, using the user's own voice?

Crosshub Inc., a company in Jeonju, Jeonbuk Province, that develops digital identity and payment technology, has built V-Pay for that moment. Led by CEO Jaeseol Kim, the company is taking part in FIX 2026 through Startup Arena 2026 and entered V-Pay, its voice biometric payment security solution, in the FIX Innovation Awards, where the application says the product was recognized.

According to Crosshub, V-Pay analyzes the voice a user speaks during payment approval, checks it against the registered user and assesses whether it may be synthesized, cloned or replayed. The company says the product brings together four functions: voice biometrics, deepfake detection, transaction risk analysis and registered-device verification. After examining the voice characteristics and the authenticity of the utterance, the system considers device information, access conditions and transaction details before making an authentication decision. Crosshub says V-Pay is not a service for executing payments by voice command. Rather, it is a security technology for steps that require identity verification, such as payments, remittances and logins.

The company says a risk-based authentication method lets the process distinguish transactions that need additional checks. It adds that V-Pay is designed to handle the authentication request, voice analysis, risk assessment, approval result and security record in one connected workflow. In Crosshub's description, users may need to enter a password or one-time code less often, while service operators can adjust the authentication step according to the risk of the device, access and transaction.

V-Pay is being developed for integration through application programming interfaces (APIs) and software development kits (SDKs) with the existing systems of financial institutions, payment gateway (PG) providers, fintech companies and e-commerce platforms. Crosshub's IDBlock digital identity solution and its B·Pay payment infrastructure provide the technical foundation for connecting V-Pay to identity verification and payment approval. The company completed a minimum viable product (MVP) in July 2026 and says it is now refining the functions needed for integration and validation in financial and payment environments. It also says it has filed or holds patents on technologies including voice-based authentication code entry and advertising-linked authentication.

The company points to a record in identity and payments that predates V-Pay. In September 2026, it received both a Gold Award and a Bronze Award at the 2026 Taiwan Innotech Expo for patent technologies related to IDBlock and V-Pay, after expert document review and on-site evaluation. In 2025, it signed a USD 1.2 million agreement to supply an identity solution to TB Tech Laos, a digital solutions company in Laos. In Vietnam, it has signed memoranda of understanding on digital student IDs with the University of Danang's University of Science and Education, Vietnam National University, Hanoi, and Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City. In Korea, it is jointly pursuing Travel Pass, an integrated payment and travel service for international visitors, with Woori Bank. Crosshub notes that these agreements concern its identity and payment services, and that V-Pay itself is still being prepared for integration and validation.

Crosshub describes Kim as a fintech founder building digital transaction infrastructure that links identity and payment processes across borders and addresses AI-driven impersonation. The company explains that users who move between countries or services often have to verify their identity again and arrange a new payment method. IDBlock supports digital identity verification, B·Pay links payment methods with services, and Travel Pass applies both to visitors to Korea, from pre-arrival preparation to payments, transportation and travel services in the country. V-Pay covers the approval step.

Its main differentiator, the company says, is a technical structure that connects identity verification, payment integration and approval security in a single user flow. Its primary customers are the digital finance, authentication and security teams at banks and payment gateway providers that serve international users or manage approval security for remote transactions. Crosshub says the end users are visitors to Korea and people who use remote payment services, and that it plans to extend its business customers to fintech and e-commerce platforms as the solutions are validated.

The company's stated reasons for exhibiting are to introduce V-Pay to financial services and AI and ICT companies and to explore partnerships for applying it in live transaction environments. At the booth, Crosshub plans to explain which risk signals V-Pay evaluates and how it connects to an existing approval process, and to ask financial institutions, PG providers, fintech firms, e-commerce businesses and platform operators about their adoption requirements. The topics include API and SDK integration, the conditions that should trigger additional authentication, how voice manipulation findings should be used, and how authentication records should be managed. Crosshub also wants to speak with international buyers about how voice-based security could work where payment methods and identity checks differ, and it says it will use the feedback to prioritize improvements and define the scope of later validation projects.

Crosshub currently exports to Laos, where it has an agreement to supply IDBlock. V-Pay is at the validation and commercialization stage for overseas use. The company's priority markets for V-Pay are Japan, China, major Southeast Asian countries and North America, with other markets to follow. It says it will review each market's payment practices and authentication requirements, run validation projects with local partners and widen supply according to the results.

The company names several hurdles. Financial and payment systems and biometric data requirements differ from country to country, so APIs and SDKs need adjusting and performance must be validated locally. Voice authentication has to account for differences in language, pronunciation and conditions of use, and the detection of synthetic and replayed voices has to be tested under varied conditions. Reviewing financial institutions' security and operating standards and finding reliable local partners may also take time. Crosshub says it intends to address them through market-by-market reviews and phased validation with local businesses.

For its plan, Crosshub says it will use the MVP to validate integration with financial institutions, PG providers, fintech companies and platform operators, starting with applying voice biometrics and deepfake detection within transaction flows. It also plans to refine the product for different languages and payment environments, move to paid adoption and commercial supply after validation, and in the longer term connect V-Pay with its identity and payment infrastructure for a wider range of financial and digital services.

Now in its third year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Technology Expo) is a future-industry exhibition that combines and links innovative technologies in future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. It runs from Wednesday, Oct. 21, to Saturday, Oct. 24, at EXCO in Daegu. Under the theme "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," the exhibition shares industry trends and core technologies through AI-based technology exhibitions, conferences and lectures by experts from Korea and abroad, and networking programs.
